# Regex fixtures for skill: improvement-miner
# Format: one directive per non-empty, non-comment line.
#   MATCH: <prompt>     — regex from config/default-triggers.json must match
#   NO_MATCH: <prompt>  — regex must NOT match
# NO_MATCH decoys pin the LEARN boundary vs outcome-review (borrowed
# verbatim from tests/fixtures/routing/outcome-review.txt) and general
# mining/mineral prose.
#
# The second MATCH block covers INTENT phrasings. The original trigger was
# self-referential -- every alternative required the caller to already know
# the skill's name or its "mine" metaphor, so it fired only if you already
# knew to ask for it (measured: 0 fires across 400 real prompts sampled from
# session transcripts). "determine improvements to the onboarding flow" and
# "examine for evidence ..." stay NO_MATCH: both embed a trigger word inside
# a longer word, which the (^|[^a-z]) guards exclude -- do not drop those
# guards.

MATCH: mine improvements
MATCH: run the improvement miner
MATCH: mine the repo for improvement evidence
MATCH: time for some improvement mining
MATCH: what should we improve
MATCH: what could we improve in this repo
MATCH: what's worth fixing next
MATCH: what is worth improving here
MATCH: find improvement opportunities
MATCH: give me improvement proposals
MATCH: sweep the repo for improvements
MATCH: scan the codebase for improvements

NO_MATCH: how did the experiment perform last week
NO_MATCH: review the cohort retention numbers
NO_MATCH: the dataset describes mineral improvements in soil samples
NO_MATCH: what did we learn from the incident
NO_MATCH: determine improvements to the onboarding flow
NO_MATCH: examine for evidence of a race condition
# Single-item triage and negations must NOT route to a repo-wide mining
# workflow. "worth fixing/improving" is anchored behind "what" for exactly
# these -- do not drop that anchor.
NO_MATCH: is this bug worth fixing before the release
NO_MATCH: that typo isn't worth fixing right now
NO_MATCH: not worth fixing, just document it
NO_MATCH: the flaky test is worth fixing
NO_MATCH: is this worth improving or should we rewrite it
NO_MATCH: how should we improve the retry logic
# The "what" anchor spans are deliberately tight ({0,6} / {0,15}). [[ =~ ]] is
# unanchored, so a "what" from an unrelated clause can otherwise bridge into a
# later "is worth fixing". Widening either span reopens this.
NO_MATCH: I know what he said is worth fixing
# "scan/sweep/comb <anything> for improvement" is NOT repo mining. The verb
# must name a repo-scope noun, and "proposal" must be plural (asking for a
# set) rather than singular (authoring one). Loosening either reopens these.
NO_MATCH: scan the diff for improvements to the error message
NO_MATCH: scan the image for improvement in contrast
NO_MATCH: sweep the logs for improvement in error rates
NO_MATCH: comb through the PR for improvement suggestions
NO_MATCH: write an improvement proposal for the API redesign
NO_MATCH: the improvement proposal from marketing needs review
